text:
olivia: FYI sampleapp onboarding started getting a lot of 429s after we flipped to the client-credits/lease flow. Seeing repeated 'lease_drop' in logs.

sam-devex: ugh. can you paste a log snippet and confirm which SDK variant (js/py)?

olivia: js. log snippet:
```json
{"ts":1715554310,"msg":"lease_drop","session":"s-123","pending":42}
```
Request pattern looks like a burst on page load (prefetch).

kai-sdk: ah — that's the new refundable-lease behavior. we tightened default lease ttl recently. the client must renew the lease within the ttl or the server returns it. are you holding the lease during multi-page fetches?

olivia: we do a debounce to coalesce prefetches (debounce=200ms). if ttl is 100ms some requests might exceed it and get dropped.

maria: that mismatch explains it. options: increase lease ttl in sampleapp, reduce debounce window, or change renew to happen in a background task. which should we recommend for onboarding docs?

sam-devex: recommend making SDK sample conservative: set leaseTtlMs to 500 in onboarding sampleapp + add a short note in quickstart about the tradeoff. also show how to opt into renew-in-background.

kai-sdk: +1. i'll open a PR to bump sample config and add a migration blurb. i'll also add a telemetry metric 'lease_renew_missed' so we can detect this pattern automatically.

nora-sre: can we add a small server-side grace window (like +100ms) while we roll this out to avoid user churn? we already have a tiny buffer but can tune if needed.

ciara-bot: deploy-bot: rollout started for sampleapp config change (canary 5%) :rocket:

olivia: thanks — i'll smoke test onboarding flow after canary lands. also can you add a quick troubleshooting snippet in dev docs for the 'lease_drop' message?

sam-devex: will add a blurb and short code sample:
```js
// workaround: increase TTL while onboarding heavy prefetch patterns
client.configure({ leaseTtlMs: 500 });
```

kai-sdk: PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/789 — includes tests, doc, and metric.

olivia: verified on canary: 429 rate reduced from ~18% -> ~0.5% after ttl bump. nice work :tada:
